solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Awe maybe after short time for cruel god (6)

indicators.note: a short time is a moment, abbreviated to MO

blocks.note: mo = a moment, as in 'half a mo'
Loch Awe is a Scottish lake, so Awe is an example of a loch

annotation.surface: Someone describes the dread they feel before a cruel god.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Awe' reads as reverence, but it is the name of a Scottish lake; 'maybe' marks it as one example of the category.
annotation.definitionFit: A proper name used as a description: the Canaanite deity to whom children were said to be sacrificed, now a byword for cruelty.

entries.clue: Wrongfully grabs material possessed by girl (15)

indicators.note: the girl owns, so holds, the material word

annotation.surface: A dispute over who took some fabric that a girl owned.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Material' looks like cloth, but it is the adjective meaning relevant, which is why it can become a word like apt or pertinent.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to take something dishonestly for one's own use, especially funds entrusted to one.

entries.clue: The French quarter divided by river moving slowly (9)

indicators.note: the river splits LA from GHETTO by sitting between them

blocks.note: a ghetto is a quarter of a city

annotation.surface: A slow river winds through the French quarter of a town.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Moving slowly' sounds like the river's current, but it is a tempo marking: the answer is a musical term.
annotation.definitionFit: A musical direction: an Italian tempo marking asking for a fairly slow pace, a little quicker than largo.

entries.clue: Idiot into sparkling wine and starchy food (7)

indicators.note: the idiot goes into the wine word

annotation.surface: A fool gets into the fizz and the stodgy food at a party.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a party, with drink and food side by side, but the wine is only a wrapper and the food is the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: a tropical root eaten as a staple and the source of tapioca, prized for its starch.

entries.clue: Make an error in space excursion? (4,2)

blocks.note: the phrasal verb for stumbling into a mistake
read literally: an outing (a journey) heading skyward

annotation.surface: An astronaut's blunder during a spacewalk.
annotation.walkthrough: The second reading is whimsical: a journey upward into space, taken word for word; the question mark flags that the phrase is being taken literally.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: the idiom for blundering, and a literal outing that goes upward into space.

entries.clue: Back cure leaving knight ready for battle again? (7)

indicators.note: the knight departs from the cure word, so N is removed

annotation.surface: A knight's bad back is cured and he is ready to fight again.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Back' looks like part of the injured knight's body, but it is a plain synonym. N is chess shorthand for knight, since K is taken by the king.
annotation.definitionFit: The prefix re- plus armed: supplied with weapons once more, so ready to fight again; the question mark flags the literal reading.

entries.clue: Greek character? Behold — half of his field is cut! (5)

indicators.note: only half the field word survives
the rest of the word is cut away

blocks.note: surface padding here, though lo = behold also gives a second route: PHI, a Greek letter, plus LO
his field of study was philosophy

annotation.surface: An exclamation about a Greek whose field has been cut in half.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Greek character' suggests a letter of the alphabet, and indeed PHI plus LO for 'Behold' also builds the answer; but the character is a person, a philosopher.
annotation.definitionFit: A person as character: Philo of Alexandria was a Hellenistic Jewish thinker who wrote in Greek.

entries.clue: How to make pear juice for media meeting? (5,10)

blocks.note: juice is made by pressing the fruit
Conference is a common British variety of pear
completes the instruction: the press makes juice

annotation.surface: A question about pear juice, oddly attached to journalists.
annotation.walkthrough: The wordplay reads as an instruction in a kitchen; the trick is knowing the pear variety, which also happens to mean a meeting.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an event where someone answers questions from the media, the press.

entries.clue: Queen and Country — first person to fall down (4)

indicators.note: in a down entry, the letter drops from the top to the bottom

blocks.note: names the pronoun I, which is also the first letter of the country: that is the letter that moves

annotation.surface: A patriotic cry for Queen and Country, then someone collapses.
annotation.walkthrough: 'First person' is both the pronoun and the first letter of the country; in this down clue, falling down moves it from the top to the foot.
annotation.definitionFit: A borrowed word: in India a rani is a queen or a rajah's wife.

entries.clue: Watery stretch coming from huge river in endless sweep (8)

indicators.note: the huge-river pair sits in the sweep word
the sweep word loses its last letter

blocks.note: brush = sweep, without its last letter H
OS = outsize, a clothing label for huge
the Po is Italy's longest river

annotation.surface: A stretch of water flows out of a mighty river in a long curve.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Huge river' reads as one thing, but splits into two parts: a clothing size and an Italian river.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by description: the strait joining the Black Sea to the Sea of Marmara at Istanbul is a long narrow stretch of water.

entries.clue: Bits of holy text in old city guarded by special force (5)

indicators.note: the special force surrounds, so guards, the city

blocks.note: SAS = Special Air Service, the British special forces regiment
Ur is the ancient Mesopotamian city

annotation.surface: Sacred manuscripts in an ancient city, protected by commandos.
annotation.walkthrough: Ur of the Chaldees is the crossword's favourite old city, worth learning as a two-letter building block.
annotation.definitionFit: A specialist term: the chapters of the Koran, so portions of a holy text.

entries.clue: A new atomiser for perfume (9)

indicators.note: the letters are made into something new

blocks.note: kept as it is, and part of the fodder

annotation.surface: A fresh spray bottle bought for scent.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Perfume' looks like a noun in the shop, but it is the verb, to scent something.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the verb: to give something a pleasant smell.

entries.clue: Language of the old man approaching John in greeting (7)

indicators.note: the old man comes up to, so stands before, the rest
the John goes inside the greeting

blocks.note: john is slang for a toilet, as is lav

annotation.surface: A father greets a man called John in some foreign tongue.
annotation.walkthrough: 'John' looks like a man's name, but it is American slang for the lavatory.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: the Middle Persian language of the Sassanid era.

entries.clue: Self-important politician in middle of room probing matter (7)

indicators.note: the politician sits in the middle letters
takes the two centre letters of room
the combined letters go into the matter word, as a probe does

blocks.note: the two centre letters of rOOm
pus = matter, as in discharge from a wound

annotation.surface: A pompous politician investigates something in the middle of a room.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Matter' looks like 'issue', but it is the medical sense: discharge from a wound.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: full of one's own importance, grandly solemn.

entries.clue: Attempt again diminished performer — one holding something back in theatre? (9)

definitions.text: one holding something back in theatre

indicators.note: made smaller, so the word loses its last letter

blocks.note: retry = attempt again, without its last letter Y

annotation.surface: A faded performer tries another comeback on stage.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Theatre' conjures the stage, which suits the actor, but the definition means an operating theatre.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by function: a surgical instrument that holds back the edges of a wound during an operation.

entries.clue: People with foreign character boarding vessels (8)

indicators.note: the character gets aboard, so inside, the vessels

blocks.note: beta is a letter of the Greek alphabet, so a foreign character

annotation.surface: Travellers with a foreign accent climbing onto ships.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Vessels' suggests ships to board, but here they are containers.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: the answer names one nation, a people of the Himalayan plateau.

entries.clue: Couple pinning medic, an idiot (5)

indicators.note: the couple holds the medic in place between its letters

blocks.note: MB = Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's qualification

annotation.surface: Two people hold down a doctor and call him a fool.
annotation.walkthrough: The medic is not a doctor's title but a degree, Bachelor of Medicine.
annotation.definitionFit: Informal slang for a stupid person, from the cartoon elephant.

entries.clue: Men hit sea — moving this? (9)

indicators.note: the letters move to new places

annotation.surface: Sailors put to sea, and the question is what they are handling.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: as the crew heads out to sea, this is the rope they are working.
annotation.definitionFit: Read straight, the clue asks what sailors adjust as they set out; the mainsheet is the rope controlling the mainsail's angle.

entries.clue: Demonstrate quietly, wander here and there (5)

annotation.surface: A protester marches silently and drifts around.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Demonstrate' tempts as a protest, but it means show to be true.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the sense of establishing something as true.

entries.clue: Green Triumph car without top has this writer in (7)

indicators.note: in a down entry the top is the first letter, which goes
'has X in' means owns X within it, so the car word keeps the writer inside itself
completes 'has ... in': the writer ends up within the car word

blocks.note: the Triumph Herald is a classic British car; HERALD loses its H

annotation.surface: A green convertible Triumph with the writer sitting inside.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Without top' fits a convertible, but it removes the first letter of the car's model name.
annotation.definitionFit: A colour named after a gem: the bright green of the precious stone.

entries.clue: Seal fibre somehow in sculptural feature (3-6)

indicators.note: the letters are arranged in some other way

annotation.surface: A seal is carved somehow from fibre in a sculpture.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Seal' looks like the animal or a stamp to press, but it is simply four of the letters to rearrange.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: carving that projects only slightly from its background, a common feature of friezes.

entries.clue: Circle or something similar, mostly feature of Dartmoor? (7)

indicators.note: most of the word, so it loses its last letter

blocks.note: an equal = something similar, without its last letter L
a tor is a rocky hilltop; Dartmoor in Devon is full of them

annotation.surface: A stone circle, or something like one, on Dartmoor.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Circle' calls up Dartmoor's stone circles, but it is a line of latitude.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: the great circle round the earth midway between the poles.

entries.clue: Permits variable amount of money to be loaned (7)

definitions.text: amount of money to be loaned

indicators.note: the letters vary their order

annotation.surface: A bank allows a flexible loan.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Variable amount' reads as one financial phrase; 'variable' is the indicator and 'amount' starts the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A specialist accounting term: a sum advanced to someone for a purpose, as with a petty cash float.

entries.clue: Work of art that is, in part, second only to Raphael (5)

indicators.note: the 'that is' letters go in the part word
takes the second letter of Raphael

blocks.note: pt = part, as in a serial's Pt 2

annotation.surface: A painting judged partly second only to Raphael's.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Second only to Raphael' reads as high praise, but it just picks one letter from the painter's name.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: a painting or sculpture of the Virgin Mary holding the dead Christ, like Michelangelo's.

entries.clue: Be right, holding rugger is for the heavy physical type (7)

indicators.note: BE and R hold the rugger letters

blocks.note: RU = Rugby Union; rugger is British slang for rugby

annotation.surface: A rugby fan insists the sport suits big, tough players.
annotation.walkthrough: The rugby surface makes the answer feel at home: the heavy type is exactly who plays in the scrum.
annotation.definitionFit: Informal description: a big, strong, aggressive person, one who gives bruises.

entries.clue: Give warning about person close to relative (4)

indicators.note: the close, so the end, of relative

annotation.surface: Someone raises a warning about a person standing near a relation.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Close to' looks like 'near', but it means the end letter of relative.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to be an omen of, to presage, which is a kind of warning.

entries.clue: Cut hole in material that’s affected by the sun outside? (9)

indicators.note: the sun word goes outside the material

annotation.surface: Someone cuts a hole in sun-bleached fabric.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Material' reads as the fabric being cut, but it is a specific cloth, a favourite crossword fabric.
annotation.definitionFit: A surgical term: to bore a hole in the skull, so the past tense of a very particular hole-cutting.

entries.clue: Commercial link-up that is needing external money (3-2)

indicators.note: the letters need something around them

annotation.surface: A business partnership that needs outside funding.
annotation.walkthrough: 'External money' sounds like outside investment; in fact the money is the wrapper round the other letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A business term: a product or promotion linked to another, such as a film's merchandise.

entries.clue: Son conveniently near to provide drink (6)

annotation.surface: A son living nearby is useful for fetching a drink.
annotation.walkthrough: A shandy is beer mixed with lemonade, a British pub staple.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: a beer and lemonade mix is one kind of drink.

entries.clue: Regional potato dish containing rodent (6)

indicators.note: the dish holds the rodent

annotation.surface: A local potato dish with a rat inside it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Potato dish' reads as one phrase, but the definition stops at 'potato'.
annotation.definitionFit: A regional word: Irish dialect for a potato, which is what 'Regional' signals.
